# The standing at a glance {#sec-standing}

*Before this chapter:* @sec-baselines (the baselines, the reference
configurations and the scoring protocol) and @sec-metrics (the error
metric). The chapters after this one give each row its context.

```{python}
#| label: para-standing-lede
#| output: asis
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
import standing as S
print(f"**On the {sum(S.DATASETS[k].fair_drive for k in S.available())} tasks it is compared on ({len(S.available())} with a standing), ISLA at its reference configuration leads on some fields, is "
      "level on others and trails on a few, and on every flow task it is the only one of the three architectures whose error "
      "does not change when the test geometry is moved or resampled.** This chapter is the evidence of Part IV on one page: one "

```

```{python}
#| label: setup-standing
#| include: false
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
import standing as S
ROWS = S.headline_rows()
```

## Every headline number {#sec-standing-table}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-thesis
#| output: asis
out = ["| dataset and task | field | ISLA error | GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA | Transolver ÷ ISLA | ISLA rotated and translated ÷ native | chapter |",
       "|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|"]
for k, f, lab in ROWS:
    s = S.Standing(k)
    cells = []
    for a in S.BASELINES:
        v = s.verdict(a, f)
        word = {"leads": "ISLA leads", "trails": "ISLA trails", "is level with": "level", "is not compared with": "not compared‡"}[v]
        if s.ds.fair_drive and f in s.ds.provisional:
            word = "no verdict§"
        cells.append(("not compared‡" if word == "not compared‡" else f"{S.fmt_ratio(s.ratio(a, f))} ({word})") if s.has(a) else "—")
    name = s.ds.name + ("†" if not s.ds.reference else "")
    out.append(f"| {name} | {s.fields[f]} | {s.err('ISLA', f):.4f} | {cells[0]} | {cells[1]} | {s.shift('ISLA', f, 'posed'):.3f} | @{s.ds.section} |")
print("\n".join(out) + "\n")
print(": The standing of the three reference configurations on every dataset with a standing artifact: ISLA's "
      "relative L2 error (@sec-metrics) on the native mesh, each baseline's error divided by ISLA's, and ISLA's own error when every test case "
      "is rotated and translated, over its native error. Seed means over two seeds, float32, the validation or test split of "
      "each dataset (@sec-splits). The words apply the book's seed rule: a lead needs every seed of one architecture below every "
      "seed of the other and the seed means at least 3% apart. How to read this: a ratio above one favors ISLA; rows are "
      "different problems and are not comparable with one another; † marks a row whose ISLA checkpoints are of the raw-read "
      "variant rather than the reference configuration (@sec-isla-normalized-reads); ‡ marks a row whose baselines read the "
      "freestream as a physical vector rather than a unit direction, so no comparison is drawn from it (@sec-de-result). "
      "Data: results/char/ (the artifact of each row is named in its chapter).")
```

## The two invariances, measured {#sec-standing-invariances}

**Move the geometry, and on every flow task only ISLA's error stays put;
redraw a surface task's surface, and again only ISLA's stays put.** Two scorings of every checkpoint test the two properties ISLA is
built for (@sec-invariances). *Rotated and translated* applies a random
rigid motion to every test case, a different one per case, and asks each
model for the field on the moved body. *Uniform point cloud* replaces the
native surface mesh by points drawn uniformly by area, at the same count,
with exact quadrature weights; it changes the scored set itself on the
three surface tasks whose meshes exceed the cell budget (DrivAerML
Surface, HiLiftAeroML, SHIFT-SUV), and nowhere else. @fig-standing-shifts
shows both, each as an architecture's error under the scoring over its own
native error.

```{python}
#| label: fig-standing-shifts
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Each architecture's own error under a changed presentation of the same
#|   test cases, over its native error, on a log scale. Top: every case
#|   rotated and translated, on every dataset. Bottom: the surface redrawn as
#|   a uniform point cloud, on the three surface tasks where that changes the
#|   scored set. ISLA blue squares, GeoTransolver red circles, Transolver
#|   amber triangles; the vertical line is no change. How to read this: these
#|   are changes of each model's own error, not comparisons between models;
#|   a baseline mark at 20 means its error is twenty times its native error.
#|   ISLA's two marks away from one, on the lug and Tensile2d, come from
#|   boundary samples that tie for nearest on those meshes (@sec-invariances).
#|   Data: results/char/.
#| fig-height: 6.4
#| code-fold: true
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8, 6.2), gridspec_kw=dict(hspace=0.35, height_ratios=[2.6, 1.0]))
for ax, protocol, lim in ((axes[0], "posed", (0.8, 900)), (axes[1], "area", (0.8, 20))):
    S.plot_shifts(ax, protocol)
    ax.set_xlim(*lim)
    ticks = [t for t in (1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500) if lim[0] <= t <= lim[1]]
    ax.set_xticks(ticks); ax.set_xticklabels([str(t) for t in ticks]); ax.minorticks_off()
axes[0].set_xlabel("rotated and translated ÷ native, own error [–]")
axes[1].set_xlabel("uniform point cloud ÷ native, own error [–]")
label_line(axes[0], 1.12, 7.3, "ISLA", BLUE, fontsize=8.5)
label_line(axes[0], 60, 7.3, "GeoTransolver", RED, fontsize=8.5, ha="center")
label_line(axes[0], 60, 6.55, "Transolver", AMBER, fontsize=8.5, ha="center")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: para-standing-invariances
#| output: asis
FLOW = [k for k in S.available() if k not in ("tensile2d", "lug", "deepjeb")]
SURF = [k for k in S.available() if "area" in S.DATASETS[k].protocols]
sh = lambda ks, archs, p: [S.Standing(k).shift(a, f, p) for k in ks for f in S.DATASETS[k].headline for a in archs]
ip = max(abs(x - 1) for x in sh(FLOW, ["ISLA"], "posed"))
bp = sh(FLOW, S.BASELINES, "posed")
ia = max(abs(x - 1) for x in sh(SURF, ["ISLA"], "area"))
ba = sh(SURF, S.BASELINES, "area")
print(f"Over every headline field of the {len(FLOW)} flow tasks, the rigid motion leaves ISLA's error within {100 * ip:.1f}% of its native value and "
      f"multiplies the baselines' by {min(bp):.0f} to {max(bp):.0f}: rotated, a model that reads coordinates is asked about a "
      "pose it has never seen, and it answers with something worse than the mean field. On the three surface tasks, every field, the uniform "
      f"point cloud moves ISLA's error by at most {100 * ia:.1f}% and multiplies the baselines' by {min(ba):.1f} to {max(ba):.1f}: "
      "a model that averages over points rather than over area answers a different question when the points move.")
```

## Where ISLA leads, where it is level, where it trails {#sec-standing-reading}

```{python}
#| label: para-standing-groups
#| output: asis
GROUPS = (("External aerodynamics, surface fields", ("drivaerml_surface", "shift_suv", "hilift")),
          ("Flow fields in the volume", ("drivaerml_volume", "airfrans")),
          ("Solid mechanics", ("lug", "deepjeb", "tensile2d")))
_ud = __import__("json").load(open(S.RES / "udrvl_210_reduction_2026-09-10.json"))["arms_fp32"]
UD = {"GeoTransolver": _ud["gt_physical_lr1e3"]["pressure_l2"] / _ud["gt_unit_lr1e3"]["pressure_l2"],
      "Transolver": _ud["transolver_physical_lr3e3"]["pressure_l2"] / _ud["transolver_unit_lr3e3"]["pressure_l2"]}
def reading(k):
    s = S.Standing(k)
    if not s.ds.fair_drive:
        return (f"{s.ds.short} is not compared: in its record the baselines read {s.ds.drive_note}"
                + (f"; in a control on this dataset at 10,000 cells (Transolver at learning rate 3e-3), the unit direction lowers "
                   f"GeoTransolver's own pressure error {UD['GeoTransolver']:.1f}-fold and Transolver's {UD['Transolver']:.1f}-fold (@sec-de-result)" if k == "hilift" else f" (@{s.ds.section})"))
    parts = []
    for word, label in (("leads", "ISLA leads"), ("is level with", "is level"), ("trails", "trails")):
        items = [f"{s.fields[f]} against {a} ({S.fmt_ratio(s.ratio(a, f))})" for f in s.ds.headline for a in S.BASELINES
                 if s.has(a) and s.verdict(a, f) == word]
        if items:
            parts.append(f"{label} on " + ", ".join(items))
    held = "".join(f"; its {s.fields[f]} ratios are given without a verdict, because {why}" for f, why in s.ds.provisional.items())
    return f"On {s.ds.in_sentence} ISLA " + "; ".join(p.replace("ISLA leads", "leads") for p in parts) + held + f" (@{s.ds.section})"
for title, keys in GROUPS:
    txt = ". ".join(reading(k) for k in keys if k in S.available())
    if title == "Solid mechanics":
        txt += (". On the lug, ISLA reads which faces are clamped, which is the hole, which half of it is loaded and the pressure "
                "on it; GeoTransolver reads the same four labels on the surface triangles, and Transolver reads none (@sec-interior-lug)")
    print(f"**{title}.** {txt}.\n")
```

## What the standing compares, and what it does not {#sec-standing-scope}

**Each architecture runs at a configuration that trains under one memory
ceiling, so the comparison is matched in memory, not in parameters.** The
three reference configurations come from candidates that train under
80 GiB per GPU on two selection datasets, the DrivAerML Surface task and
the 210-wing HiLiftAeroML set; the registered selection rule named no
single configuration for both datasets, and each pick has the smallest joint score over the two
(@sec-selection). No architecture's pick, ISLA's included, is its most
accurate candidate on the car, and for the baselines the wing scores that
decided it are scores under the freestream in inch/s (@sec-selection). The three spend their
memory differently, as @tbl-standing-cost shows: at similar memory, ISLA
carries several times GeoTransolver's parameters.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-standing-cost
#| output: asis
out = ["| dataset and task | | ISLA | GeoTransolver | Transolver |", "|---|---|---:|---:|---:|"]
for k in S.available():
    c = {a: S.cost(k, a) for a in S.ARCHS}
    if not all(c.values()):
        continue
    out.append(f"| {S.DATASETS[k].name} | parameters [millions] | " + " | ".join(f"{c[a]['n_parameters'] / 1e6:.1f}" for a in S.ARCHS) + " |")
    out.append(f"| | training peak memory [GiB per GPU] | " + " | ".join(f"{c[a]['peak_gib']:.0f}" for a in S.ARCHS) + " |")
print("\n".join(out) + "\n")
print(": The resources of the three reference configurations on each task: trainable parameters and the training peak device "
      "memory per GPU (maximum over four GB300 GPUs, bfloat16 autocast). How to read this: the three are matched by the memory "
      "ceiling of the selection rule, not by parameter count; ISLA carries several times GeoTransolver's parameters at similar "
      "memory. Instrument: one-epoch runs of the reference configurations with the raw slice reads, which have the same "
      "parameters and the same tensors as ISLA; the time per epoch of each is in its dataset chapter. "
      f"Data: results/char/{S.COST_FILE}.")
```

The standing is a statement about these three configurations on these
splits with two seeds each. It does not say that ISLA would lead at equal
parameter count, nor how the comparison moves with the training set's size
(@sec-capacity has the scaling evidence, on smaller ISLA configurations).
It does not cover AeroZoo, the benchmark with held-out families of bodies
and enclosures. Its comparisons with GeoTransolver are measured with inputs
that AeroZoo's rule classes as labels, so they are provisional
(@sec-aerozoo-allowed), and its standing is an open question of
@sec-open-questions.
Every scope statement is collected in @sec-limits.
